newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SocGen buys 51 pct stake in SAfrica broker.
newsitem.headline: SocGen buys 51 pct stake in SAfrica broker.

text.p: French bank Societe Generale (SocGen) announced on Wednesday that it had acquired a 51 percent stake in stockbroking firm Frankel Pollak.
The new company would be known as Societe Generale-Frankel Pollak (Pty) Ltd (SGFP).
The move would ensure that SocGen becomes the largest foreign-owned local banking operation in South Africa employing more than 350 people, the bank said in a statement.

SocGen managing director Peter Gray said the acquisition of Frankel Pollak marked an important strategic development for the French banking group which has been developing an extensive investment banking network and operation in emerging markets world-wide, such as Asia.
"South Africa, like Asia, is becoming increasingly attractive to international banks and financial houses.

"And, while many of these institutions are still deciding whether or not to focus attention on the South African market, SocGen has already established a headstart with the acquisition of a local bank in 1991 followed now by Frankel Pollak," Gray said.
Frankel Pollak chief executive officer Sidney Frankel said the deal would enable it to better develop tailor-made products and technology that suited its clients' individual requirements.

The company would also have the financial muscle to underwrite and place international issues in overseas markets for South African corporates given the partial and potential complete lifting of exchange control.
Frankel would become a member of the Advisory Board of SocGen Johannesburg and would fill the position of deputy chairperson and chief executive officer of SGFP.
Gray would become a director of SGFP, while Leslie Frankel, currently chairperson of Frankel Pollak would become life president of the new venture.
Yves Tuloup of SocGen Paris would be made chairperson.
